parks: McMichael Canadian Art Collection
Gallery just south of the village core, known for its Group of Seven collection.
Bindertwine Park
Kleinburg's largest park, in the East Humber River valley east of the village.
Humber River trails
Forested valley trails for hiking and biking around the village.
Kortright Centre for Conservation
Nature and conservation centre on the East Humber River, a short drive south.

Part of the Humber trail system, linking south toward Boyd Conservation Area.
shopping: Islington Avenue village core
Historic main street with local shops, cafés and restaurants.
The Doctor's House
Well-known restaurant and event venue in the village.
Nashville Road and Major Mackenzie Drive
Everyday services for the newer Kleinburg-Nashville neighbourhoods.
Vaughan Mills

kleinburg.commute: Kleinburg sits near Highway 27 and Major Mackenzie Drive. Highway 427 now runs north to Major Mackenzie Drive (opened in 2021), giving a fast route to Highway 407 and Highway 401. York Region Transit buses serve the area, and Vaughan Metropolitan Centre, the north end of TTC Line 1, is a short drive away. The closest GO train is Maple GO on the Barrie line.
changing: Highway 427 extension
In 2026 Ontario began looking for builders to extend Highway 427 north from Major Mackenzie Drive to the future Highway 413.
Kleinburg-Nashville growth
New subdivisions and parks are planned or under way west of the village.
pockets: Kleinburg village core
Walkable historic main street. Suits buyers who want character and village life.
Nashville
Quiet hamlet next to Kleinburg. Suits buyers who want space with services nearby.
Kleinburg-Nashville subdivisions
Newer homes near Nashville Road and Major Mackenzie. Suits families wanting a newer house.
kleinburg.family_answer: Yes. Kleinburg has public and Catholic elementary schools right in the village, plus trails along the Humber River, Bindertwine Park and the McMichael gallery close to home. New parks are planned as the Kleinburg-Nashville area grows.
kleinburg.commute_answer: By car, take Highway 427 south from Major Mackenzie Drive to Highway 407 or Highway 401, then into the city. By transit, get to Vaughan Metropolitan Centre station and ride TTC Line 1 south to Union Station.

Father John Kelly Catholic Elementary School
St. Joan of Arc Catholic High School
parks: Maple Community Centre and Library
On Keele Street, with a pool, arena, gym and library, renovated in 2022.
Canada's Wonderland
Amusement park on the south edge of Maple.
Eagle's Nest Golf Club

shopping: Maple village core
Local shops and services around Keele Street and Major Mackenzie Drive.
Vaughan Mills
Large indoor mall at Highway 400 and Rutherford Road.
Promenade Shopping Centre
Mall serving Maple and Thornhill.
maple.commute: Highway 400 runs through Maple with interchanges at Major Mackenzie Drive and Rutherford Road. Maple GO Station on Station Street is on the Barrie line, with trains about every 15 to 30 minutes in the morning rush. YRT routes 26 Maple, 20 Jane, 107 Keele, 85 Rutherford and 4 Major Mackenzie serve the area, and route 26 connects to Vaughan Metropolitan Centre on TTC Line 1.
changing: Barrie line expansion at Maple GO
Metrolinx is adding a second track, new platforms and more parking toward all-day, two-way GO service.
pockets: Maple village core
Older homes near Keele and Major Mackenzie. Suits buyers who want to walk to the GO train.
Hope and Teston
Northern Maple. Suits buyers wanting a quieter, more open setting.
Sherwood
On the Maple and Concord border. Suits buyers wanting quick access to Highway 400 and Vaughan Mills.
maple.family_answer: Yes. Maple has public and Catholic elementary and high schools, the Maple Community Centre and Library with a pool and arena, and Canada's Wonderland next door. Highway 400 and Maple GO make commuting easy for working parents.
maple.commute_answer: By car, take Highway 400 south from Major Mackenzie Drive or Rutherford Road. By transit, take the Barrie line GO train from Maple GO to Union Station, or YRT route 26 to Vaughan Metropolitan Centre and TTC Line 1 downtown.

caledon-bolton.commute: Bolton is about 50 km northwest of downtown Toronto. Highway 427 is about 9 km southeast and Highway 400 about 14 km east, with Highway 50 and Highway 9 running through the area. Brampton Transit route 41 serves Bolton, and GO buses connect Caledon to the Kitchener line.
changing: Highway 413
Construction began in Caledon in 2025 on the new highway linking Highway 400 and Highway 401/407 in Halton.
New Caledon East Public School
Peel DSB broke ground in December 2024, with opening planned for September 2026.
Caledon growth plan
The town's Official Plan expects the population to grow from about 80,000 to 300,000 over 30 years.
pockets: Bolton
Caledon's largest community. Suits families wanting a walkable downtown and newer subdivisions.
Caledon East
Small village with trails and a community complex. Suits buyers wanting quiet.
Palgrave
Rural hamlet on the Caledon Trailway. Suits buyers wanting acreage.
Mayfield West
Newer community in south Caledon. Suits commuters heading toward Brampton.
caledon-bolton.family_answer: Yes. Bolton has public and Catholic elementary schools, a middle school and two high schools, Humberview and St. Michael. Trails like the Humber Valley Heritage Trail and nearby Albion Hills give families room outdoors.
caledon-bolton.commute_answer: Most people drive, taking Highway 427 or Highway 400 south toward Toronto. Brampton Transit route 41 serves Bolton, and Caledon has GO bus connections to the Kitchener line.

Historic main street with specialty shops and cafés.
king-city-nobleton.commute: King City is about 40 km north of downtown Toronto, with Highway 400 at King Road (exit 43). King City GO Station on the Barrie line is the township's train station, and Metrolinx is adding a second platform, a pedestrian bridge and more parking for future all-day service. GO buses serve Nobleton and King City.
changing: King City GO Station upgrades
New west platform, pedestrian bridge and parking as part of Barrie line GO expansion.
pockets: King City
The township's largest village, with the GO station. Suits commuters who want village living.
Nobleton
Small town with an arena and plazas. Suits families wanting a close-knit community and big lots.
Schomberg
Historic main street village. Suits buyers wanting a walkable small-town feel.
Kettleby and the countryside
Rural hamlets and estates. Suits buyers wanting acreage and quiet.
king-city-nobleton.family_answer: Yes. King City and Nobleton each have public and Catholic elementary schools, King City Secondary serves the whole township, and private options include Villanova College and The Country Day School. The township also has over 100 km of public trails.
king-city-nobleton.commute_answer: Drive south on Highway 400 from King Road, or take the Barrie line GO train from King City GO to Union Station.

East Gwillimbury has no high school yet; students attend Newmarket schools such as Huron Heights. Check boundaries with YRDSB.

Town parks

Yonge Street and Green Lane, with Loblaws, Michaels and PetSmart.

Large enclosed mall on Yonge Street in Newmarket.
sharon-east-gwillimbury.commute: Highway 404 runs north to Woodbine Avenue near Ravenshoe Road, and Yonge Street and Green Lane link to Newmarket. East Gwillimbury GO Station on Green Lane is on the Barrie line, with weekday trains to Union Station taking about an hour. Newmarket GO is also close by.
changing: New schools in Queensville
Queensville Elementary opened in 2025, and a new Catholic elementary school is planned for September 2027.
York Region sewage works
New sewer and pumping station work in East Gwillimbury, scheduled for 2028 to 2030, to support growth.
pockets: Sharon
Historic village with the Sharon Temple and sports complex. Suits buyers wanting quiet and heritage character.
Queensville
Growing community with new schools. Suits families wanting newer homes.
Holland Landing
On the East Holland River. Suits buyers who love the outdoors and the water.
Mount Albert
Village of about 4,900. Suits buyers wanting a small-town, rural feel.
sharon-east-gwillimbury.family_answer: Yes. East Gwillimbury has public and Catholic elementary schools in each village, including the new Queensville Elementary that opened in 2025, plus the Sharon Temple, Rogers Reservoir and more than 40 town parks. High school is in nearby Newmarket.
sharon-east-gwillimbury.commute_answer: Take the Barrie line GO train from East Gwillimbury GO or Newmarket GO to Union Station, about an hour. By car, take Highway 404 south.

Humber River Recreation Trail

Yorkdale Shopping Centre

toronto.commute: Subway Line 1 serves Yorkdale and the northwest, and Line 2 serves Bloor West Village. UP Express runs from Union to Pearson every 15 minutes, stopping at Bloor and Weston. GO's Milton and Lakeshore West lines serve Kipling, Mimico and Long Branch. Line 6 Finch West and Line 5 Eglinton are now open, and the Gardiner, QEW, 401 and 427 handle drivers.
changing: Line 6 Finch West
Opened December 2025: 18 stops from Finch West station to Humber College.
Line 5 Eglinton
The Eglinton Crosstown opened to riders in February 2026.
Ontario Line
Under construction, with tunnelling under way and opening expected in the early 2030s.
pockets: Humber Valley Village
Etobicoke, near James Gardens. Suits families wanting larger homes and green space.
Bloor West Village
Walkable shopping street with subway access. Suits families wanting a village feel in the city.
The Junction
Lively and walkable. Suits buyers who want patios and independent shops.
Etobicoke waterfront (Humber Bay)
Condos by the lake. Suits buyers wanting lake views and quick highway access.
Humber Summit
Northwest Toronto beside Vaughan. Suits buyers wanting Toronto close to Woodbridge.
toronto.family_answer: Yes. Toronto's west end has big parks like High Park and James Gardens, the Humber River trail, four publicly funded school boards and walkable main streets like Bloor West Village and The Junction.
toronto.commute_answer: From the west end, take subway Line 2 or Line 1 downtown, or a GO train from Kipling, Mimico or Long Branch to Union Station. UP Express from Bloor or Weston reaches Union in a few stops.

woodbridge.commute: Woodbridge sits between Highway 400 and Highway 27, with Highway 7 running through it and Highway 407 just south. The closest GO trains are Rutherford and Maple on the Barrie line, and GO buses also serve the area. YRT routes connect to Vaughan Metropolitan Centre and Pioneer Village stations on TTC Line 1.
changing: Barrie line GO expansion
Metrolinx is adding a second track and station upgrades at Maple GO toward all-day, two-way service.
Highway 427 extension and Highway 413
Ontario is moving ahead in 2026 with extending Highway 427 north and building the Highway 413 east section.
Cortellucci Vaughan Hospital
Opened in 2021 on Major Mackenzie Drive, Vaughan's first hospital.
pockets: Sonoma Heights
1990s and 2000s homes near Islington and Major Mackenzie. Suits families wanting detached homes and townhomes.
Islington Woods
Larger lots and bigger homes. Suits move-up buyers wanting space.
Weston Downs

Woodbridge core
Walkable older village around Woodbridge Avenue, with condos nearby. Suits buyers wanting a main street.
Vellore Village
Newer homes at Weston and Rutherford. Suits families wanting a newer house.
woodbridge.family_answer: Yes. Woodbridge has many public and Catholic schools, including Holy Cross Catholic Academy, an IB World School, plus Boyd Conservation Park, the Kortright Centre and the Woodbridge Pool and Memorial Arena close to home. Woodbridge Avenue and Market Lane cover everyday shopping.
woodbridge.commute_answer: By car, take Highway 400 or Highway 427 south toward downtown Toronto. By transit, take YRT to Vaughan Metropolitan Centre or Pioneer Village and ride TTC Line 1, or take the Barrie line GO train from Rutherford or Maple.

Vaughan Mills

vellore.commute: Vellore Village sits just west of Highway 400, with access at Rutherford Road, Major Mackenzie Drive and Teston Road. The nearest GO trains are Rutherford and Maple on the Barrie line. YRT routes connect to Vaughan Mills Terminal and on to Pioneer Village and Vaughan Metropolitan Centre stations on TTC Line 1.
changing: Barrie line GO expansion
Metrolinx is adding a second track and station upgrades at Maple GO toward all-day, two-way service.
Highway 427 extension and Highway 413
Ontario is moving ahead in 2026 with extending Highway 427 north and building the Highway 413 east section.
Cortellucci Vaughan Hospital
Opened in 2021 on Major Mackenzie Drive, Vaughan's first hospital.
pockets: Vellore Village
Newer homes near Weston and Rutherford. Suits families wanting modern homes near the community centre.
Vellore Woods
Townhomes and detached homes. Suits buyers wanting parks and ponds close by.
Sonoma Heights
Next door in Woodbridge. Suits families wanting established detached homes.
vellore.family_answer: Yes. Vellore Village has a community centre with a pool and rink, parks like Vellore Woods Park and Matthew Park, public and Catholic elementary schools close by, and Tommy Douglas and Emily Carr for high school.
vellore.commute_answer: By car, take Highway 400 south toward downtown Toronto. By transit, take YRT to Vaughan Metropolitan Centre or Pioneer Village and ride TTC Line 1, or take the Barrie line GO train from Rutherford or Maple.
